Emily — thanks for the clear questions. Short answer: our SOC 2 Type II (2026 period) covers hosted API endpoints and Redwood-managed Dedicated pools; Private/VPC/on-prem deployments are generally out of scope for the standard report unless we onboard them into the audit boundary as a managed offering.

A few clarifications for your team:
- Hosted API: in-scope; you can reference the Type II report and the tested control descriptions.
- Dedicated (reserved pools): covered when the pool is provisioned and operated by Redwood (single-tenant logical isolation is not an automatic exclusion). Our sample selection included Dedicated pools serving customer workloads during the audit window.
- Private/VPC: typically out-of-scope if the customer controls networking and hosts the inference nodes; however, if the customer uses Redwood’s managed control plane and we provide operational management (patching, backups, KMS integration) then certain control areas may still be in-scope.

We can provide a bridge letter that explains exactly which hosting configurations were tested and which were not, plus recommended compensating evidence for VPC deployments. I’ve looped in Laura (security/compliance) and Jordan (solutions) to confirm what artifacts we can share and whether the Dedicated pool used by Atlas earlier this quarter was part of the SOC sampling.

I’ll follow up with a short packet (SOC cover page + bridge letter template + a hosting matrix).

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Ben / Jordan — quick grounds rules for responses to procurement:

2) For Dedicated pools: if the customer’s Dedicated pool was active during the audit period and our control testing included that environment, we can list it as in-scope. We should reference the hosting-matrix spreadsheet that documents which pools were sampled.
3) For VPC or on-prem: provide a bridge letter describing what controls in the Type II report are relevant, what evidence we can supply (e.g., patching records, change-management logs, KMS attestations), and note any control owners that shift to the customer.
